text.title: embeddings-evaluation Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns specific to embeddings-evaluation. Each has a description, an observable detector and a concrete repair.

failure-mode.description: LLM-generated query-document pairs are the primary evaluation signal; recall numbers are inflated because the queries paraphrase the passages they were generated from.
failure-mode.detector: Golden-set rows lack a `source` field or every row reads `synthetic`; Recall@10 above 0.95 for every candidate; queries contain no typos, abbreviations or domain jargon; no usage-log export in the prerequisites.
failure-mode.repair: Rebuild the set from real queries (logs or SME-written); keep synthetic rows only as a flagged, separately reported augmentation. Rule r-real-queries-not-synthetic.

failure-mode.description: Candidates are compared only on price per million tokens and latency; quality is never measured, or is measured after the cheapest model has already been chosen.
failure-mode.detector: The report has a cost table and no metric table, or the recommendation names a model that is not the top on any quality metric without stating a quality floor.
failure-mode.repair: State the quality floor first, measure Recall@K / MRR@10 / nDCG@10 for every candidate, then choose the cheapest model above the floor. Rule r-quality-floor-before-cost.

failure-mode.description: The golden set has 10 to 30 queries; every model's confidence interval overlaps every other's and the ranking changes between runs.
failure-mode.detector: Reported query count below 50; bootstrap CI width on nDCG@10 wider than the gap between first and last place; the ranking flips when one query is removed.
failure-mode.repair: Grow the set to at least 50 real queries (target 50 to 500) before reporting a ranking; until then report "insufficient data", not a winner. Rule r-golden-set-min-50.

failure-mode.description: Models are ranked on one metric, usually Recall@50 or cosine similarity to a "correct" passage, and the model that wins it loses badly on the top-5 ordering the RAG pipeline actually consumes.
failure-mode.detector: The report has one metric table; K in Recall@K does not match the production retriever's top-k; MRR or nDCG is absent.
failure-mode.repair: Report all three metrics with K equal to production top-k, one ranked table each, and read the trade-off explicitly. Rule r-three-metrics-minimum.

failure-mode.description: Chunk size, query-rewriting prompt or a fine-tuned embedder was tuned while watching the same golden set the headline numbers are computed on; the reported score is an upper bound production never reaches.
failure-mode.detector: No hold-out split is named in the report; fine-tuning data contains golden-set passage ids; offline nDCG is far above what production click-through implies after deployment.
failure-mode.repair: Hold out 20% of queries before any tuning, compute headline numbers on the hold-out only, and audit fine-tuning data against hold-out ids. Rule r-holdout-20.

failure-mode.description: A winner is declared from point estimates that differ by under a point; the re-index and migration cost is spent on a gap a re-run could reverse.
failure-mode.detector: The report shows means without confidence intervals; no bootstrap or paired test is mentioned; the gap between the top two is under 1.5 points on the primary metric and the recommendation still names a winner.
failure-mode.repair: Bootstrap 95% CIs over queries, paired test between the top two; if not separated, escalate to a live A/B with click-through telemetry instead of shipping. Rule r-significance-gate.
